topic: log-volume of hulls and the size of the indeterminacy
claim_A: the indeterminacy must be absorbed by hulls; if absorbing it costs too much, the resulting bound is vacuous
source_A: Scholze-Stix (the l^2-level loss objection), as summarised in research/controversies.md C01
claim_B: the log-volume is taken on the hull of the possible images, so the indeterminacy is inside the object being measured rather than multiplying it afterwards
minimal_disputed_statement: does the hull-of-images operation keep the log-volume small enough to yield a non-vacuous inequality?
what_would_settle_it: an explicit computation of the hull log-volume for one q-pilot, with the indeterminacy included
